problem_statement:
Bug #28699403: SHOW GRANTS THROW ERROR FOR EXISTING SESSION WHEN
MANDATORY_ROLES CHANGED
RB#22429

When the user calls SHOW GRANTS and does supply an USING clause
the roles in that clause need to be checked if they're actually
granted to the user.

However when there is no USING clause the list of active roles from
the session's sec context is used as a default.

This is a list that (since it's a static copy done at session init
and updated at SET ROLE) can contain "stray" roles, i.e. ones that
were granted to the user at the time the list was created, but revoked
since the list was created.

The situation is even further complicated since the list of "granted"
roles does also include the list in the mandatory roles variable.

Thus just using the list of active roles as a default for the
USING clause will cause errors for such stray roles that are no
longer in the list of currently granted roles for that user.

This is a valid problem in the way the list of active roles is
maintained into the sec context.
But the good part is that the actual privilege checks always intersect
that list with the list of the currently granted roles when checking
privileges.
Thus in normal privilege checks the stray roles in the active roles
list have no effect.

Thus the only issue remaining is also ignoring them during SHOW GRANTS.
This basically means that we don't have to check if roles are usable
unless we have a proper USING clause specified by the user.

The fix adds a flag to notify the checking function that the USING
list is actually the default one from the sec context so that
it can skip the roles check.

Test case added.
